news.headline: Pershing Square Discloses $2.1B Microsoft Stake, Dumps Alphabet
news.body: Bill Ackman revealed on May 15 that Pershing Square built a $2.1 billion position in Microsoft (MSFT), citing a 'highly compelling valuation' at 21x forward earnings after shares fell ~15% YTD. Ackman simultaneously exited his long-held Alphabet stake to fund the move, calling Microsoft's M365 and Azure 'two of the most valuable franchises in enterprise technology.' MSFT rose ~3% intraday on the disclosure. Markets care because a concentrated Ackman position signals deep conviction on AI monetization and Azure growth at a dislocation price.

news.headline: Figma Surges 9-15% After 46% Revenue Beat, Full-Year Guidance Raised
news.body: Figma (FIG) reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $333.4 million, up 46% YoY and well above the $313–316M consensus, with adjusted EPS of $0.10 vs. $0.06 expected. The company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance by ~$55 million to $1.422–1.428 billion and reported net dollar retention of 139%, a two-year high. Shares surged up to 15% intraday on May 15, recovering from a 52-week low of $16.60 hit in late April. The results counter the bear thesis that AI competition from Google and Anthropic would erode Figma's core design software demand.

news.headline: Cerebras (CBRS) Falls 10% on Day 2 After Historic 68% IPO Debut
news.body: AI chipmaker Cerebras Systems (CBRS) shed roughly 10% on May 15, a day after surging 68% in its Nasdaq debut to close at $311.07, giving it a ~$95 billion market cap on the first day. The IPO raised $5.55 billion — the largest U.S. tech IPO since Uber in 2019 — pricing at $185/share and opening above $350. The day-2 pullback reflects typical post-IPO profit-taking, but markets are closely watching Cerebras as a bellwether for the AI infrastructure investment cycle and a potential pipeline of major AI IPOs including SpaceX and OpenAI.

news.headline: Cisco Surges 13-15% on Record Q3 Revenue, AI Orders Hit $9B Target
news.body: Cisco (CSCO) reported fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $15.84 billion (+12% YoY), beating the $15.56B estimate, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.06 vs. $1.04 expected; Q4 guidance of $16.7–16.9B revenue far exceeded Wall Street's $15.82B forecast. Management raised FY26 AI hyperscaler order expectations to $9 billion and announced a restructuring cutting fewer than 4,000 jobs to redirect investment toward AI, silicon, and optical. Shares jumped 13–15% in their sharpest single-day rally since 2002, with HSBC upgrading the stock and raising its price target to $137. The print repositions Cisco as a structural AI infrastructure beneficiary, not just a legacy networking name.

news.headline: Brown-Forman Rejects Sazerac's $15B Takeover Bid, Leaving Company Without Suitor
news.body: Brown-Forman (BF.B), maker of Jack Daniel's and Woodford Reserve, rejected a $32/share all-cash offer from privately held Sazerac — backed by Wells Fargo and Apollo Global Management — that valued the spirits group at approximately $15 billion, a significant premium to its ~$26 market price. The Brown family, which controls voting shares, declined the bid after Pernod Ricard merger talks also collapsed in late April, leaving the company without any active acquisition partner. Shares slipped as the rejection removed the M&A premium and raised questions about the company's standalone strategy amid declining U.S. alcohol consumption and ongoing sales headwinds. The failed deal would have created an American whiskey colossus combining Jack Daniel's, Buffalo Trace, and Blanton's.

news.headline: Samsung Electronics Slides Up to 9.3% as Union Reaffirms 18-Day Strike Plan
news.body: Samsung Electronics' South Korean labour union confirmed it would proceed with an 18-day strike beginning May 21 involving over 41,000 chip division workers, rejecting the company's offer of unconditional wage talks and saying it would only return to negotiations after June 7. Samsung shares fell as much as 9.3% on May 15, compared with a 7.0% decline in the benchmark KOSPI, as analysts flagged mounting risks to production continuity and delivery reliability at the world's largest memory chipmaker. SK Hynix also plunged 7.7%, with the two stocks together accounting for a record 42.2% of the KOSPI weighting. Foreign investors net sold approximately 5.6 trillion won of Korean equities on the day, extending a seven-session selling streak.

news.headline: KOSPI Breaches 8,000 Then Crashes 6.1% in Historic Intraday Reversal
news.body: South Korea's KOSPI surged past the landmark 8,000 level for the first time in early trade on May 15, buoyed by AI-driven momentum and optimism over the Trump-Xi summit, before collapsing 488 points, or 6.12%, to close at 7,493.18 — its largest single-session decline in months. The reversal was driven by confirmation that U.S. chip export controls were not discussed at the bilateral Beijing meeting, combined with the Samsung strike risk and profit-taking after a near-vertical rally that pushed the index's P/E ratio above the S&P 500's. The small-cap Kosdaq fell more than 5% to 1,129.82, while net foreign outflows topped 5.6 trillion won. Analysts at Daishin Securities attributed additional selling pressure to the end of Q1 earnings season removing a key catalyst.

news.headline: Kioxia Posts 92.7% Profit Surge, Plans U.S. ADS Listing; Shares Retreat on Profit-Taking
news.body: Tokyo-listed Kioxia Holdings reported a 92.7% jump in annual operating profit to 870.4 billion yen for FY ending March 2026, beating estimates, and forecast Q1 FY2027 operating profit of 1.3 trillion yen ($8.2 billion) — far above consensus — on surging AI-driven NAND demand. The company simultaneously announced preparations to list American Depositary Shares on a U.S. exchange to broaden its investor base, a strategic move reflecting its market cap now exceeding Sony and Fast Retailing. Despite the blowout results, Kioxia shares fell approximately 6.8–8.3% on May 15 as broader Japanese tech stocks were caught in the region-wide chip selloff triggered by the KOSPI rout and the absence of chip-export relief from the Trump-Xi summit. The stock remains up roughly 300% year-to-date.

news.headline: Nikkei Drops 2% as Japan PPI Hits 4.9%; BOJ June Hike Odds Climb to 77%
news.body: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.99% to close at 61,409 on May 15, while Japan's 10-year JGB yield climbed to around 2.7% — its highest in nearly a decade — after April producer prices rose 4.9% year-on-year, sharply accelerating from March's 2.9% and well above the 3% forecast. BOJ board member Kazuyuki Masu called for policy rates to be raised "as soon as possible," reinforcing market pricing of a 77% probability of a BOJ rate hike at the June meeting. Major Nikkei decliners included Fujikura (-8.4%), Kioxia (-8.3%), and Advantest (-7.9%), with semiconductor names hit hardest. Rising borrowing-cost expectations amplified the negative sentiment from the global chip sector selloff.

news.headline: Trump-Xi Summit Delivers No Chip Deals; HSI Falls 1.6%, China Markets Slide
news.body: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index fell 1.6% and China's CSI 300 dropped 1.12% on May 15 after the three-day Trump-Xi Beijing summit concluded with no concrete agreements on semiconductor export controls, rare earths, or tariff reductions beyond vague pledges of wider market access. U.S. Trade Representative Greer confirmed chip export controls were "not a major topic of discussion" at the bilateral meeting, dashing investor hopes that had partially driven the prior week's Asian equity rally. Xi's warning that Taiwan independence could trigger U.S.-China "clashes and even conflicts" added a geopolitical risk premium to Chinese assets. Analysts noted the summit prioritized managing tensions rather than a structural reset, with Goldman Sachs maintaining an overweight on Chinese equities but flagging limited near-term catalysts.

news.headline: Brent Surges >5% on Week as Hormuz Stays Shut; IEA Warns Supply Deficit Until Oct
news.body: Brent crude futures strengthened above $106/bbl Friday, booking a weekly gain of over 5%, as diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran conflict stalled and the Strait of Hormuz remained effectively closed. The IEA warned crude and fuel flows through the Strait fell ~4 million bpd in March-April, with the global oil market likely to remain materially undersupplied through October even if conflict resolves next month. Saudi Arabia separately informed OPEC its output had dropped to the lowest level since 1990, compounding supply fears. The EIA's May STEO assessed Middle East production shut-ins at 10.5 million bpd in April, projecting global inventory draws of 2.6 million bpd for 2026.

news.headline: Copper Slumps ~5%, Gold Hits March Low Below $4,500 on Rate-Hike Inflation Fears
news.body: Copper fell nearly 5% Friday while gold dropped to its lowest level since March, sliding below $4,500/oz, as war-driven inflation fears sparked a broad metals selloff. Investor concerns mounted that surging inflation—fueled by the Hormuz closure and Middle East conflict—could force global central banks to raise borrowing costs and suppress economic growth, dragging industrial and precious metals simultaneously. Bond yields rose globally as the dollar extended its longest winning streak since March, pressuring commodities priced in greenbacks. Gold has now lost over 5% in the past four weeks from its record highs above $5,500/oz.

news.headline: Gold Posts Weekly Loss as Hot US PPI, Rate-Hike Odds Squeeze Bulls
news.body: Gold fell below $4,700/oz for a second straight session on May 14, heading for a weekly decline after US producer prices in April surged at their fastest pace since early 2022, driven by energy and trade costs linked to the Iran war. Combined with the prior session's CPI print of 3.8% — a three-year high — markets fully priced out Fed rate cuts for 2026, with CME FedWatch now pricing a ~30% chance of a December hike. The opportunity cost pressure on non-yielding bullion is squeezing speculative longs, even as structural central-bank demand (244 tonnes in Q1 2026) remains firm.

news.headline: NGSA Sees Record 40.3 Bcf/d Summer Gas Power Burn on Coal Switching, Data-Center Load
news.body: The Natural Gas Supply Association's 2026 Summer Outlook, released May 14, projects U.S. natural gas power burn reaching a record 40.3 Bcf/d this summer, driven by low prices accelerating coal-to-gas switching and surging baseload demand from data centers. LNG exports are forecast to rise 4.3 Bcf/d year-on-year to 19.9 Bcf/d as new capacity from Plaquemines, Corpus Christi Stage 3, and Golden Pass Train 1 comes online. Despite robust supply of ~117 Bcf/d, total summer storage injections are forecast at only 1,772 Bcf versus 2,210 Bcf last summer, leaving end-of-season inventories ~106 Bcf below the five-year average and tightening the winter risk picture. Henry Hub futures near $2.88/MMBtu reflect a market pricing in below-average storage builds, with coal displacement adding structural demand that markets will monitor into Q3.

news.headline: India Doubles Gold & Silver Import Duty to 15%, Sparking Bullion Market Chaos
news.body: India's government raised effective import duties on gold and silver from 6% to 15% on May 13, doubling basic customs duty on gold to 10% and hiking the agriculture cess fivefold, pushing total levies to 18.45% including IGST. MCX gold futures surged 5.74% in a single session while silver briefly crossed ₹3 lakh per kg—a gain of over ₹17,000/kg overnight. The move was triggered by a ballooning precious-metals import bill of $102.5 billion in FY2025-26 and pressure on India's current account amid the West Asia crisis and a rupee that hit a record low of ₹95.75 per dollar. Global silver on COMEX rose ~2.1% in sympathy while analysts warned the duty reversal could revive smuggling and distort trade flows through the India-UAE CEPA quota route.
